_comment: ILLUSTRATIVE — the interface contract the Program Architect would compute for the Approach-3 (sequenced) program. NOTE the key difference from Approach 2: the contract carries only the invariants KNOWABLE UP FRONT (the customer intent, logging, naming, destination). The downstream match SOURCE is deliberately NOT here — it is a runtime value (the edge NAT pool) delivered by inter-pipeline chaining, not a contract constant. A pipeline child reaching execution without this contract still FAILS LOUD (INTERFACE_CONTRACT_MISSING); the DAG edges carry the runtime piece the contract cannot.

endToEndIntent._note: This is the customer intent — knowable up front, so it IS in the contract. What each downstream hop actually MATCHES on the wire (the post-NAT source) is NOT here (see addressing).

addressing.postNatSource: RUNTIME — chained from the edge-fw leg's report.md, NOT a contract constant
addressing._note: This is the crux of Approach 3. The edge SNATs the partner CIDR to a pool it picks from live edge state during design; dmz-sg and core-fw must match THAT pool. Because the pool is an output of the edge design, it cannot be resolved into a static contract constant — it rides the DAG edge (inter-pipeline chaining) instead. If it could be pre-agreed, this would be Approach 2.

sequencing.chained: the upstream leg's report.md (the chosen NAT pool + post-NAT flow) into the downstream leg's §6
sequencing.settledness: F18 predicate holds the downstream leg until the upstream deliverable is fully persisted
sequencing._note: DESIGN order is edge-first (the NAT pool must be chosen before downstream can match it). This is NOT the apply order — see acceptance.applyOrderRecommended.

consistency.noAsymmetricHoles: Every hop permits EXACTLY the flow for its correct source (edge: pre-NAT partner CIDR; dmz/core: the post-NAT pool) and denies anything broader; return traffic is the established/related session, never a separate broad inbound permit. Node C blocks the program if any leg widens the flow, matches the WRONG source stage (pre- vs post-NAT), or adds a return-path hole.

perDeviceSlice.edge-fw: untrust -> dmz permit for the flow (match pre-NAT partner CIDR) + source-NAT partner CIDR -> pool (tag PARTNER-SNAT-2026) + explicit deny + log. DELIVERABLE MUST publish the chosen pool (it is the chained input downstream needs).
perDeviceSlice.dmz-sg: aws_security_group.dmz_app ingress from the POST-NAT pool (chained from edge-fw) tcp/443; egress to 10.20.0.10/32 tcp/443; NO 0.0.0.0/0 and NO partner-CIDR ingress (that would be the pre-NAT source — wrong stage).
perDeviceSlice.core-fw: dmz -> inside ASA access-list line matching the POST-NAT pool -> app (+ explicit deny + log).

acceptance.applyOrderVsDesignOrder: DESIGN order is edge-first (NAT pool chosen first); APPLY order is core-first (innermost hop provisioned first so the outer hop is never opened before the inner hop is ready). These are DIFFERENT and both correct — a classic Approach-3 teaching point.
